standards.name: Minimum Information About a Bioactive Entity (MIABE)
standards.abstract: MIABE is a community reporting guideline for publications and data deposits describing bioactive entities (small molecules, therapeutic proteins, peptides, antibodies, carbohydrates, and related compounds) and their biological activities. It focuses on pre-clinical (or equivalent) data and the minimum information that should be included to allow data reuse, comparison and reanalysis. The standard was developed by representatives from pharmaceutical companies, data resource providers and academic groups (published as a MIABE paper in Nature Reviews Drug Discovery) and is presented as a simple checklist of information to include in final publications, not as a prescriptive experimental protocol or a formal database schema.

classification.rationale: The source material repeatedly describes MIABE as a 'simple checklist' and guidance of items to report in publications (prose/checklist form) rather than a formal field-level metadata schema. While example 'sample MIABE file' tables appear in the supplement, the core MIABE product is presented as reporting guidance (instructions of what to include), so it should be classified as a PRINCIPLE.

principles.principle: Describe cellular assays: cell type, culture conditions, reagent/agonist information, titration/replicate details, and observed results or toxicological observations.
principles.evidence:
Cellular Assays
Cell type Human erythrocytes, infected with Plasmodium falciparum NF54
Culture conditions Parasites cultivated in medium consisting of RPMI 1640 supplemented with 0.5% ALBUMAX II, 25mM Hepes, 25mM NaHCO3 (pH7.3), 0.36mM hypoxanthine and 100mg/mL neomycin ... Cultures maintained in atmosphere of 3% O2, 4% CO2, 93% N2 in humidified modular chambers at 37ºC.
Agonists/antagonists Compounds dissolved in DMSO (10mM) and diluted in hypoxanthine-free culture medium. Titrated in duplicates over a 64-fold range in 96 well plates.
Results IC50 = 9nM IC50 = 0.2nM 5156 (Figure 2) + 5158 (Table 3)

principles.principle: Report whole-organism and in vivo study details: animal model, disease model, dosing route and schedule, formulation/delivery details, and results.
principles.evidence:
Whole Organism Studies
Animal studies In vivo antimalarial activity. Female NMRI mice (20-22g).
Disease models Plasmodium berghei infected mouse model (strain GFP ANKA)
Dosing route Intravenous infection with parasite, oral dosing with compound
Dosing schedule Compounds formulated with 10% ethanol, 30% PEG400 and 6% vitamin E TPGS and administered in a volume of 10mL/kg as either a single dose (24h post infection) or three consecutive daily doses (24, 48 + 72h post infection)
Results Single dose: reduced parasitemia on day 3 by 99.9%, prolonged survival time to 10.7 days; Multiple dose: 99.6%, prolonged surv

principles.principle: Specify the scope and entity types covered by MIABE and that it is intended for pre-clinical data reporting.
principles.evidence:
Scope of MIABE
Entity types – small molecules, therapeutic proteins, peptides and antibodies, carbohydrates
Drugs, herbicides, pesticides, nutraceuticals
Pre-clinical (or equivalent) data only – clinical data well regulated, documentation defined (though little published), would require separate document written by specialists

standards.notes: Extraction focused on the MIABE checklist/guidance and the supplementary example file. The supplementary material contains a sample tabular 'MIABE file' illustrating many concrete fields (used here as evidence of checklist items) but the primary MIABE product is presented as reporting guidance (checklist), not a prescriptive table or DAG.

standards.name: PSI-MI (PSI-MI XML 2.5 schema and MITAB / controlled vocabularies)
standards.abstract: PSI-MI describes molecular interaction data (protein–protein, protein–small molecule, protein–nucleic acid, etc.). Data can record interactions observed in vitro or in vivo, with supporting metadata such as detection method, host organism, experimental role and cross-references. The standard is maintained by the HUPO Proteomics Standards Initiative (PSI) Molecular Interactions working group and comprises: an XML exchange schema (PSI-MI XML 2.5 / 3.0), tabular exchange formats (PSI-MITAB variants), and a set of controlled vocabularies (the PSI-MI CV and related CVs). It also provides validator tools and mapping/config files that encode the concrete column names and semantic constraints used by data providers and indexers (PSICQUIC, IMEx, IntAct).

classification.rationale: The source materials present concrete, field-level tabular specifications (MITAB headers and TSV mapping files) that name independent data columns (e.g. "ID(s) interactor A", "Interaction detection method(s)", "Taxid interactor A", "Confidence value(s)") and provide machine-readable mappings/validation rules. These are genuine tables (column headers and mapping TSVs), so the standard is represented here as a table.

ID_interactor_A.name: ID(s) interactor A
ID_interactor_A.descr: Stable identifier(s) for interactor A (database:identifier form, e.g. uniprotkb:Q9XYZ).

raw_full_info.example_header: #ID(s) interactor A     ID(s) interactor B      Alt. ID(s) interactor A Alt. ID(s) interactor B Alias(es) interactor A  Alias(es) interactor B  Interaction detection method(s) Publication 1st author(s)       Publication Identifier(s)       Taxid interactor A      Taxid interactor B      Interaction type(s)     Source database(s)      Interaction identifier(s)       Confidence value(s)

ID_interactor_B.name: ID(s) interactor B
ID_interactor_B.descr: Stable identifier(s) for interactor B (database:identifier form).

raw_full_info.example_header_fragment: ID(s) interactor A     ID(s) interactor B

Alt_ID_interactor_A.name: Alt. ID(s) interactor A
Alt_ID_interactor_A.descr: Alternative identifier(s) for interactor A (secondary accessions, other DBs).

raw_full_info.example_header_fragment: Alt. ID(s) interactor A Alt. ID(s) interactor B

Alias_interactor_A.name: Alias(es) interactor A
Alias_interactor_A.descr: Text aliases / names for interactor A (gene names, synonyms, display labels).

Alias_interactor_B.name: Alias(es) interactor B
Alias_interactor_B.descr: Text aliases / names for interactor B.

Interaction_detection_method.name: Interaction detection method(s)
Interaction_detection_method.descr: Method(s) used to detect the interaction; annotated with PSI-MI controlled vocabulary terms (e.g. MI:0018 'two hybrid').

raw_full_info.notes: The validator and mapping TSVs map detection methods to interaction types (e.g. InteractionDetection2InteractionTypes.tsv).

Publication_first_author.name: Publication 1st author(s)
Publication_first_author.descr: First author(s) of the publication describing the interaction.

Publication_identifier.name: Publication Identifier(s)
Publication_identifier.descr: Bibliographic identifier(s) for the supporting publication (e.g. pubmed:123456).

Taxid_interactor_A.name: Taxid interactor A
Taxid_interactor_A.descr: Host organism taxon for interactor A (NCBI Taxonomy id), often encoded as taxid:NNN(...).

Taxid_interactor_B.name: Taxid interactor B
Taxid_interactor_B.descr: Host organism taxon for interactor B (NCBI Taxonomy id).

Interaction_type.name: Interaction type(s)
Interaction_type.descr: Biological type of interaction, annotated with PSI-MI CV terms (e.g. physical association, direct interaction).

Source_database.name: Source database(s)
Source_database.descr: Database(s) providing the interaction (e.g. intact, mint). Often encoded as PSI-MI database CV terms.

Interaction_identifier.name: Interaction identifier(s)
Interaction_identifier.descr: Stable identifier(s) assigned to the interaction record by the source database (e.g. intact:EBI-5606332).

Confidence_value.name: Confidence value(s)
Confidence_value.descr: Scores or confidence annotations associated with the interaction (free text or controlled scheme, e.g. author-score:C).

Expansion_method.name: Expansion method(s)
Expansion_method.descr: Expansion/normalization method used for complexes (e.g. spoke, matrix); used when complex-level data are expanded into binary pairs.

Biological_role_interactor_A.name: Biological role(s) interactor A
Biological_role_interactor_A.descr: Biological role annotation for interactor A (PSI-MI CV terms).

Experimental_role_interactor_A.name: Experimental role(s) interactor A
Experimental_role_interactor_A.descr: Experimental role annotation for interactor A (PSI-MI CV terms: bait/prey/neutral/etc.).

Interactor_type_A.name: Type(s) interactor A
Interactor_type_A.descr: Interactor type for interactor A (e.g. protein, small molecule) using PSI-MI CV term.

Xref_interactor_A.name: Xref(s) interactor A
Xref_interactor_A.descr: Cross-references for interactor A (external DB accessions).

Annotation_interactor_A.name: Annotation(s) interactor A
Annotation_interactor_A.descr: Free-text annotations attached to interactor A (e.g. isoform comments, figure legend notes).

Host_organism.name: Host organism(s)
Host_organism.descr: Host organism(s) in which the experiment was performed (NCBI Taxonomy terms).

Interaction_creation_date.name: Creation date
Interaction_creation_date.descr: Date the interaction record was first created in the source database.

Interaction_update_date.name: Update date
Interaction_update_date.descr: Date the interaction record was last updated in the source database.

Negative_flag.name: Negative
Negative_flag.descr: Boolean flag indicating a negative interaction (true/false).

Feature_interactor_A.name: Feature(s) interactor A
Feature_interactor_A.descr: Feature annotations on interactor A (binding regions, mutations, ranges); can include ranges/start/end and CV terms.

Identification_method_participant_A.name: Identification method participant A
Identification_method_participant_A.descr: Method used to identify the participant (e.g. sequence tag identification, nucleotide sequence identification) -- PSI-MI CV term.

standards.notes: This extraction focuses on the MITAB/MI TAB column-level definitions and associated controlled vocabulary usage visible throughout the source files (MITAB example headers and mapping/TSV rule files). The PSI-MI standard also includes XML schema and programmatic validators (not expanded here into separate DAG/principle forms because the source presents concrete tabular field names and mapping tables).
